reason: The cited evidence shows that very rapid cooling (melt-spinning) yields an amorphous structure (E3) and that atomic size mismatch and phosphorus addition enhance glass-forming ability (E1, E2). However, none of the cited passages provide any evidence for the effects of a two-stage quench, an isothermal hold near Tg, or the proposed relaxation-mediated suppression of nucleation. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the provided references.
premises: Ultra-rapid initial quench (≥10^5 K/s) can suppress crystallization in this alloy.
A brief isothermal hold near Tg (5–30 ms) allows local structural relaxation without significant nucleation.
Local structural relaxation reduces nucleation sites and increases the kinetic barrier for crystallization.
A subsequent rapid quench can 'lock in' the relaxed amorphous structure.
The two-stage protocol will increase amorphous fraction and raise crystallization onset temperature relative to conventional quenching.
